items.title: Harishchandras and Yudhishthiras are extinct: Madras HC raps GST officials
items.summary: Claims made by Goods and Services Tax (GST) officials cannot be accepted at face value and must be supported by verifiable record, the Madras High Court said recently [Bhima Enterprises v. Principal Chief Commissioner GST]. Justice GR Swaminathan made the observation while dealing with a petition challenging a search warrant issued by tax authorities on the ground that it lacked a Document Identification Number (DIN). A circular issued by the Central Board of Indirect Tax and Customs said that no search authorisation, summons, arrest memo, inspection notices and letters issued in the course of any enquiry shall be issued by its officers without a computer-generated DIN. The Court ruled that an officer who cites technical difficulties for failing to generate the mandatory DIN must produce evidence to substantiate the claim. While emphasising the need for evidence to back such claims, the Court referred to figures from Hindu scriptures who were known for practicing honesty and righteousness. “ Harishchandras and Yudhishthiras have become an extinct species. items.title: Kerala High Court bats for full-fledged lab at Pamba to test quality of food served at Sabarimala
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently said that it was high time that a full-fledged food testing laboratory was established at Pamba to ensure prompt quality checks of Aravana, Appam (sacred food offerings) and other food items supplied at the Sabarimala temple [ Dr Mahendra Kumar PS v The State of Kerala & ors and connected case ]. A Division Bench of Justice Raja Vijayaraghavan V and Justice KV Jayakumar took note of concerns that the existing food testing laboratory at Pamba was not equipped to conduct a detailed and continuous testing of such food items. The Court was told that samples of food items had to be transported to laboratories at Pathanamthitta or Thiruvananthapuram for analysis. The Court observed that such an arrangement was not enough to ensure fast and effective quality control of the food items at Sabarimala. " We are of the considered view that it is high time that a fully fledged and comprehensive food testing laboratory is established at Pamba itself, so that the requisite tests can be conducted there without delay, thereby ensuring strict compliance with food safety standards, " the Court added.
